version.value: Wind-ensemble transcription attributed to Wenzel Sedlak, adapted for the Marine Band’s Grand Scenes recording
version.note: The booklet explicitly says the attribution to Sedlak has not been conclusively proved. The overture comes from a fifteen-movement suite preserved at the Augustinian monastery in Brno. For this recording, the flute part was modified using Rossini’s orchestral part, two added trumpet parts were removed, and contrabassoon and string bass reinforced the bass. This is a small wind ensemble with double bass, not Rossini’s original full orchestral scoring.

value.name: United States Marine Band
value.role: wind ensemble with contrabassoon and double bass

performers.note: The booklet marks the players participating in the Rossini: flute, two oboes, two B-flat clarinets, two bassoons, contrabassoon, two horns and string bass. No trumpet or cello performance is attributed to this transcription.

credits.value: Original editing and mastering: Bob Katz, Digital Domain. Wikimedia Commons upload: TonyTheTiger.
credits.note: The booklet separately credits producers Denis R. Burian and Michael J. Colburn, and recording engineers Karl J. Jackson and Kevan D. Lewis. These original production credits are distinct from the later Commons upload and MP3 conversion.

date.note: The original capture medium and dates of mastering and Ogg conversion are not documented. Commons records the current Ogg upload on 14 April 2011; that is not a recording-session date.

processing.value: Ogg Vorbis file on Wikimedia Commons, with a Commons-hosted MP3 transcode.
processing.note: The file page credits the Marine Band’s web audio as its source. The exact intervening conversion settings, original capture chain, equalisation and any noise processing are not established.

digital.format: MP3 transcode of the Commons Ogg Vorbis file

composition.value: The historical composition and the arrangement used on this album are identified as public domain.
composition.note: Rossini died in 1868. The official booklet states that its selections are public domain unless otherwise noted; it places no copyright exception on this overture. The qualified Sedlak attribution is retained rather than treating uncertain authorship as proof of rights.
